newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA cuts French car market estimate.
newsitem.headline: PSA cuts French car market estimate.

text.p: Carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen has lowered its estimate for the French car market to 1.85 million sales this year, a 13 percent fall from 2.13 million in 1996.

"Since October, we continue to have monthly order declines of between 20 and 22 percent," PSA chairman Jacques Calvet told a business dinner on Tuesday night. "We haven't seen a favourable evolution at the order level."

The market has been weak since the expiry on September 30 of a state new-cars-for-old rebate scheme, which bolstered 1996 sales. The PSA group's previous estimate for the French market for 1997 was 1.87 million car sales.
Calvet said the company has raised its estimate for the Italian car market, buoyed by a national rebate scheme, to 2.13 million sales this year from 1.74 million in 1996.
For western Europe, France included, the PSA group estimates a 2.5 percent rise in car sales this year, Peugeot Automobiles deputy director Frederic Saint-Geours said.
